messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test `testNodeSetOperations` asserts an XPath expression involving node-set and number comparison, expecting behavior consistent with the XPath specification. According to the current bug report, the problem lies in the binary operator behavior involving node-sets. The specification says that when both operands are node-sets, the comparison should be true if there is a pair of nodes (one from each set) whose string-values satisfy the comparison condition.

The relevant code in `CoreOperationCompare.equal(EvalContext, Expression, Expression)` performs the comparison. It computes the left and right operand values; if either is a node set (represented by Iterators), it dispatches to either `contains` or `findMatch` methods. Notably, `findMatch(Iterator lit, Iterator rit)` tries to find if any node in the left set matches any node in the right set by iteration. It collects all left nodes into a set, then for each right node, calls `contains(left.iterator(), rit.next())` to test for a match.

The fault is in `findMatch`: it converts the left nodes to a HashSet, then passes a new iterator from the HashSet combined with each right node to `contains`. This invokes `contains` on a fresh iterator each time with `rit.next()`. This approach can fail because `contains` likely performs string comparison on the nodes for the binary operation but gets a fresh iterator of left nodes each time and compares them directly to the right node, without properly performing the string-based comparison required.

The specification demands comparing string-values, but the current `findMatch` relies on `contains` which probably does not align with that semantic for node-sets of strings. This results in incorrect boolean evaluation of comparisons involving two node-sets.

In summary, the bug is that the `findMatch` method implements node-set comparison incorrectly by using `contains` in a way that fails to compare string-values of nodes as per the XPath spec, leading to incorrect results for binary operators involving two node-sets. The failing test reveals this mismatch because it invokes such an operation expecting XPath-compliant behavior.

Recent bug reports are not related to this issue and do not provide clues. The main insight comes from the current bug report and inspection of `CoreOperationCompare.equal` and `findMatch` implementations.

The issue should be fixed in `CoreOperationCompare.findMatch` and possibly associated comparison methods to correctly implement node-set to node-set comparison by explicit string-value evaluation. 

Methods to fix:
- `CoreOperationCompare.findMatch(java.util.Iterator, java.util.Iterator)`
- `CoreOperationCompare.equal(org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.EvalContext, org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.compiler.Expression, org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.compiler.Expression)`

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
